title: a chat merge authorization is recorded with its expiry, and the autopilot warns firstmate an hour before it lapses, listing what could still merge
acceptance: Why. On 2026-10-04 the captain's chat authorization ran to 08:00, but T-176 was carded, green and unmerged at 08:10. Nothing told firstmate the window was closing: the authorization existed only in the chat. The captain approved fixing this on 2026-10-04 ("…影響體驗正確性的都修掉").

Record. firstmate records a time-boxed merge authorization with `bin/fm-decide.sh --authorize-merges --until <ISO-8601 with offset> --quote "<the captain's words>"`. It is stored under the session state (not in any repository) with the time it was recorded. A new record replaces the previous one. `--authorize-merges --show` prints the current window, or none. This changes nothing about how merges happen: they still go only through a board card, answered by the captain or by firstmate within the window. The record is evidence and a timer, not a bypass.

Warn. While a window is open, the autopilot queues one wake 60 minutes before it closes (or at once, if less than 60 minutes remain when it is recorded): 'merge authorization ends at <time>'. The wake lists:
- pending merge cards
- PRs with a bound APPROVE and green CI, but no card
- PRs still in review or worker rounds
At expiry it queues one wake, 'merge authorization ended', so firstmate stops answering merge cards. Both wakes fire once per window, and a restart does not repeat them (T-172 boundary).
Docs. skills/firstmate/SKILL.md says firstmate records every chat merge authorization this way the moment it is given, and answers merge cards only inside a recorded window.

Tests (fail first, with a clock stub):
- recording, then 61 minutes before expiry, gives no wake
- 60 minutes before expiry gives one wake with the three lists
- expiry gives one wake
- a restart repeats neither
- a replaced window resets the warnings
Evidence is the required GitHub check and the six gates. Workers do not run the suites.
